title: Assignment 2 · Recommenders
summary: Solve the two missing ratings with user-based collaborative filtering and a latent-factor model, keeping normalization and dot-product prediction separate.
objectives: Mean-center known ratings before cosine similarity
Use neighbourhood similarity to estimate a missing rating
Complete latent factors and compute a dot-product prediction

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Assignment 2 supplies the exact matrix and latent-factor tasks; Lecture 3 motivates the representation and MMDS labels collaborative filtering depth.

sections.title: User-based collaborative filtering
sections.body: Subtract each user’s row mean from known ratings before calculating cosine similarity. The centering step makes the comparison focus on rating pattern rather than absolute generosity.

sections.title: Latent-factor prediction
sections.body: The latent-factor task uses a reconstructed rating $\hat r_{xi}=q_x\cdot p_i$ and chooses missing entries in $Q$ and $P^T$ so known ratings have zero reconstruction error. Do not reuse the neighbourhood estimates as latent factors.

math.name: Latent-factor rating
math.purpose: Predict a user–item rating from the learned user and item vectors.
math.explanation: The dot product $\hat r_{xi}=q_x\cdot p_i$ is a model prediction; it is different from a neighbourhood-weighted average.

algorithmNotes.problemDefinition: Estimate a missing user-item rating from users whose observed rating patterns overlap with the target user.
algorithmNotes.assumptions: Known ratings are comparable after centering, enough overlap exists to define neighbours, and similarity weights are used consistently.
algorithmNotes.coreInvariant: Similarity compares deviations from each user's own mean; raw generosity or harshness must not dominate the neighbourhood evidence.
algorithmNotes.formulaAlgorithm: Compute each user's mean, center known ratings as $r_{ui}-\bar r_u$, calculate cosine similarity on the centered values, and combine neighbour evidence for the missing rating.
algorithmNotes.failureModes: Common mistakes: using raw ratings before cosine similarity, treating missing entries as zeros, or confusing neighbourhood prediction with latent-factor prediction.

algorithmNotes.problemDefinition: Predict a missing rating from compact latent vectors for the user and item.
algorithmNotes.assumptions: User and item factors have compatible dimensions, the factor representation is learned from known ratings, and the prediction path is separate from neighbourhood weighting.
algorithmNotes.coreInvariant: The model uses one consistent user vector and item vector for each prediction; known ratings constrain reconstruction rather than defining a new neighbourhood.
algorithmNotes.formulaAlgorithm: Predict with $\hat r_{ui}=q_u\cdot p_i$ by multiplying matching latent coordinates and summing their products.
algorithmNotes.failureModes: Common mistakes: reusing mean-centered neighbour estimates as factors, mixing vector dimensions, or forgetting that a dot product is a model prediction.

contrastDrills.prompt: Two users rate the same items with the same relative pattern, but one user gives every item two extra stars. Why center ratings before cosine similarity?
choices: To compare preference deviations rather than different rating baselines
To make every rating equal to zero
To turn user-based filtering into a latent-factor model
To remove all missing entries from the matrix
contrastDrills.explanation: Subtracting each user's row mean removes the generosity or harshness baseline, so cosine similarity focuses on how ratings deviate from each user's own average.
contrastDrills.misconception: Using raw ratings and mistaking an absolute rating scale for a preference pattern.
contrastDrills.repair: Compute each user's mean first, subtract it from known ratings, then compare the centered vectors.
